evals.name: session-bootstrap-context
evals.prompt: I want to start working on backlog tasks for this project. Get set up.
evals.expected_output: Calls the get_backlog_context MCP tool once first to load workflow instructions, valid statuses, and the board — before listing or editing anything.
expectations: Called the get_backlog_context MCP tool as the first backlog action
Did not shell out to a `backlog` CLI (none exists)
Relied on get_backlog_context for the project's valid status-lane names rather than guessing

evals.name: create-task-via-mcp
evals.prompt: Add a backlog task titled 'Write release notes' to this project.
evals.expected_output: Calls the task_create MCP tool (or POST /api/tasks) with title set and the resolved project; does NOT run a CLI or hand-write a task .md file.
expectations: Used the task_create MCP tool (or POST /api/tasks REST) with title 'Write release notes'
Passed a project argument on the call
Did not shell out to a `backlog` CLI
Did not create or edit a task markdown file by hand

evals.name: list-tasks
evals.prompt: Show me the tasks in this backlog project.
evals.expected_output: Calls the task_list MCP tool (or GET /api/tasks) with the resolved project rather than reading task files or using a CLI.
expectations: Used the task_list MCP tool (or GET /api/tasks REST)
Passed a project argument
Did not enumerate tasks by reading the tasks directory directly
Did not shell out to a `backlog` CLI

evals.name: edit-status-and-assignee
evals.prompt: Task 1's status should be 'In Progress' and it should be assigned to me. Update it.
evals.expected_output: Calls task_edit (or PUT /api/tasks/1) setting status and assignee; does NOT open or edit the task .md file, and does NOT use a CLI.
expectations: Used the task_edit MCP tool (or PUT /api/tasks/:id) to set status and assignee
Passed a project argument and the task id
Did not open, read, or write the task markdown file to make the change
Did not shell out to a `backlog` CLI

evals.name: check-ac-array
evals.prompt: Mark the first two acceptance criteria on task 1 as complete.
evals.expected_output: Calls task_edit with acceptanceCriteriaCheck: [1, 2] (a single array of 1-based indices); does NOT edit checkboxes in the file, use repeated flags, or a CLI.
expectations: Used task_edit with acceptanceCriteriaCheck passed as an array of indices, e.g. [1, 2]
Used 1-based indices in a single array (not two separate calls, not a CLI repeated-flag form)
Did not toggle the checkbox by editing the task markdown file

evals.name: multiline-notes-array
evals.prompt: Add implementation notes to task 1 with three separate lines: 'Investigated root cause', 'Added a regression test', and 'TODO: monitor staging'.
evals.expected_output: Calls task_edit with notesAppend as an array of three strings (one per line); does NOT pass a single string with literal \n, and does NOT use a CLI.
expectations: Used task_edit with notesAppend (or notesSet) to add the notes
Passed the three lines as an array of strings (one element per line)
Did not rely on a literal \n sequence inside one string to create line breaks
Did not shell out to a `backlog` CLI

evals.name: project-resolution-from-config
evals.prompt: Using the backlog for THIS repo, list its open tasks. The repo's spec/project.yaml has `backlog_project: acme-web`.
evals.expected_output: Calls task_list with project = 'acme-web' (resolved from spec/project.yaml), rather than omitting the project or using an unrelated default.
expectations: Passed project = 'acme-web' (the value from spec/project.yaml:backlog_project) on the call
Did not omit the project or rely on an ambient/default project
Resolved the project from workflow config (spec/project.yaml), consistent with env override precedence

evals.name: claim-next-ready-task
evals.prompt: Claim the next ready backlog task and assign it to @claude.
evals.expected_output: Calls task_next (or get_backlog_context with claim/agent) with agent '@claude'; does NOT manually list-then-edit as a substitute, and does NOT use a CLI.
expectations: Used the task_next MCP tool (or get_backlog_context with claim=true) to atomically claim the next ready task
Passed the agent '@claude' so the claimed task is assigned
Passed a project argument
Did not shell out to a `backlog` CLI
